title: Eludite settings file
description: Eludite's settings (PLAN.md 4.12), one JSON object of dotted keys. Two files are merged, user then solution, so a key in the solution's file wins: the user file `settings.json` in Eludite's config directory (`$XDG_CONFIG_HOME/eludite/settings.json`, default `~/.config/eludite/settings.json`, on Linux; `%APPDATA%\eludite\settings.json` on Windows; `~/Library/Application Support/eludite/settings.json` on macOS; `ELUDITE_CONFIG_DIR` replaces the `eludite` folder), and `.eludite/settings.json` beside the open solution (or in the open folder), which a team may commit. A key missing from both has the default given here. An environment variable named by `x-eludite-env` overrides both files while it is set. Eludite watches both files and applies a change without a restart; it writes them only for eludite.settings.set (and the Options dialog, which runs it). Every property has a default, a description, a section of the Options dialog (`x-eludite-section`, in VS's Tools > Options tree), a label (`x-eludite-label`) and, for strings, how the dialog edits it (`x-eludite-editor`: text or path; `enum` gives a choice). A setting that belongs to the workspace rather than the person (`x-eludite-scope`: `solution`) is written by the Options dialog in the workspace's `.eludite/settings.json`; every other one in the user file. Unknown keys are ignored and reported.
x-eludite-sections: Projects and Solutions > Build and Run

keyboard.preset.description: The keyboard mapping scheme. Only Visual Studio's exists (PLAN.md 8); the Rider and VS Code presets come with the keymap editor.
keyboard.preset.x-eludite-label: Apply the following additional keyboard mapping scheme

build.beforeRun.description: F5 (Start Debugging) and Ctrl+F5 (Start Without Debugging) build the startup project first and launch only when the build succeeds (Visual Studio's "On Run, when projects are out of date: Always build"). MSBuild's incremental build makes an up-to-date project cost a check, not a compile. false: launch the last build as it is.
build.beforeRun.x-eludite-section: Projects and Solutions > Build and Run
build.beforeRun.x-eludite-label: On Run, build the startup project first

build.onSave.description: Build the saved file's project (or the solution, for a file in no project) after each save.
build.onSave.x-eludite-section: Projects and Solutions > Build and Run
build.onSave.x-eludite-label: Build the project after saving one of its files

build.showOutputOnStart.description: Bring the Output window forward, showing the Build source, when a build starts.
build.showOutputOnStart.x-eludite-section: Projects and Solutions > Build and Run
build.showOutputOnStart.x-eludite-label: Show Output window when build starts

build.showErrorListOnFailure.description: Bring the Error List forward when a build finishes with errors.
build.showErrorListOnFailure.x-eludite-section: Projects and Solutions > Build and Run
build.showErrorListOnFailure.x-eludite-label: Always show Error List if build finishes with errors

build.cargoPath.description: The cargo executable that builds Cargo workspaces. Empty: `cargo` on PATH.
build.cargoPath.x-eludite-section: Projects and Solutions > Build and Run

debugger.netcoredbgPath.description: The netcoredbg executable that debugs .NET programs. Empty: beside the eludite executable, then PATH (tools/netcoredbg/fetch.sh prints one).

debugger.monoPrefix.description: The prefix of the Mono that runs and debugs .NET Framework programs on Linux and macOS (the folder holding `bin/mono`). Empty: `mono` on PATH (its prefix is two folders up from the resolved executable), then `~/.local/opt/mono-root/usr`, `/usr`, `/usr/local` and `/Library/Frameworks/Mono.framework/Versions/Current`. Mono is located, never bundled: `mono-devel` on Debian and Ubuntu, `mono` on Arch, the Mono framework on macOS. Applies to the next session.
debugger.monoPrefix.x-eludite-label: Mono prefix (.NET Framework on Linux and macOS)

debugger.monoAdapterPath.description: The Mono soft-debugger adapter `eludite-dbg-mono.exe` (or the folder holding it), run by the located Mono to debug .NET Framework programs on Linux and macOS. Empty: beside the eludite executable (`eludite-dbg-mono/eludite-dbg-mono.exe`, then `eludite-dbg-mono.exe`). `dotnet build dotnet/Eludite.slnx` builds it to `debuggers/mono/Eludite.Debugger.Mono/bin/Debug/net472/`. Applies to the next session.

debugger.lldbDapPath.description: The LLDB debug adapter that debugs Cargo packages (Rust): lldb-dap from LLVM, or CodeLLDB's `adapter/codelldb`. Empty: `lldb-dap`, then `lldb-dap-22` down to `lldb-dap-15` on PATH, `/usr/lib/llvm-22/bin/lldb-dap` down to `llvm-15`, `xcrun --find lldb-dap` on macOS, then CodeLLDB (`ELUDITE_CODELLDB`, or `codelldb/adapter/codelldb` beside the eludite executable). Located, never bundled: `lldb-18` on Debian and Ubuntu, `lldb` on Fedora and Arch, Xcode on macOS, LLVM's installer on Windows (tools/lldb-dap/README.md). Applies to the next session.

debugger.rustFormatters.description: Show Rust values as Rust (`"hello"` for a String, `size=3` for a Vec, `Some(5)`, an enum by its variant) by loading the Rust toolchain's LLDB formatters (`<sysroot>/lib/rustlib/etc/lldb_lookup.py`, as rust-lldb does) into lldb-dap at launch; the sysroot is `rustc --print sysroot` in the Cargo workspace, so rust-toolchain.toml is honored. Off: LLDB's C-style view of the same values. Applies to the next session.
debugger.rustFormatters.x-eludite-label: Show Rust values with the toolchain's LLDB formatters

debugger.allowAgentsByDefault.description: Whether a new debugging session lets agents drive it (start, resume, step, change values): what Debug > Allow Agents to Drive starts with in each session. Off: an agent may read a session but not drive it until the person turns the toggle on. Applies to the next session.
debugger.allowAgentsByDefault.x-eludite-label: Allow agents to drive new debugging sessions

debugger.launchBrowser.description: Open a web project's page when it starts (F5, Ctrl+F5), as its launch profile's `launchBrowser` asks. Off: no page opens unless the start names `browser` (Debug > Start in External Browser). Applies to the next start.
debugger.launchBrowser.x-eludite-label: Open the launch profile's page when a web project starts

debugger.attachBrowser.description: Debug a web project's page too (brief 0038): when F5 opens the page in the Web Browser window, vscode-js-debug attaches to its tab once the page is up, as a second session beside the server's, so breakpoints in the page's `.ts` and `.js` files stop it. Off: only the server is debugged (attach to the tab later with Debug > Attach to Browser Tab...). Applies to the next start.
debugger.attachBrowser.x-eludite-label: Debug the page's JavaScript when a web project starts

debugger.nodePath.description: The Node.js executable vscode-js-debug runs on (brief 0038; version 18 or later). Empty: `node` on PATH, then Volta's (`~/.volta/bin/node`), nvm's default (`~/.nvm/alias/default`) and fnm's default (`~/.local/share/fnm/aliases/default`, `~/.fnm/aliases/default`). Located, never bundled. Applies to the next session.

debugger.jsDebugPath.description: vscode-js-debug's DAP server, `src/dapDebugServer.js` (or the folder of the unpacked release holding it), which debugs pages in the Web Browser window (brief 0038). Empty: `~/.cache/eludite/js-debug/<version>/js-debug/src/dapDebugServer.js` (what tools/js-debug/fetch.sh unpacks, the version in tools/js-debug/PIN), then `js-debug/src/dapDebugServer.js` beside the eludite executable. Located, never bundled. Applies to the next session.

languageServers.rustAnalyzerPath.description: The rust-analyzer executable for Cargo workspaces. Empty: beside the eludite executable, then PATH, then `rustup which rust-analyzer`. Applies to the next rust-analyzer started.

test.runSettings.description: A .runsettings file for .NET tests (Visual Studio's Test > Configure Run Settings): VSTest projects get its contents as the RunSettings of every discovery and run; Microsoft.Testing.Platform test applications get `--settings <path>`. A relative path is under the solution's folder. Empty: none.

test.parallel.description: Run tests in parallel (Visual Studio's Run Tests In Parallel, off by default): VSTest runs its test assemblies side by side (`MaxCpuCount` 0); `cargo test` runs a package's tests on several threads, so only a failed test's output is shown (libtest captures the others'). Off: `cargo test` runs one test at a time with `--test-threads=1 --nocapture`, so every test's output is its own. Microsoft.Testing.Platform frameworks keep their own parallelization settings.

test.vstestConsolePath.description: The vstest.console.dll that discovers and runs VSTest projects (xunit 2, NUnit and MSTest projects that have not moved to Microsoft.Testing.Platform), run with `dotnet`. Empty: the one in the newest .NET SDK `dotnet --list-sdks` lists.

git.enabled.description: Git integration (brief 0040): the Git Changes and Git Repository windows, the status glyphs in the Workspace window and on document tabs, the status bar's branch and sync arrows, and the editor's change margin. Off: Eludite reads no repository and eludite.git.* fails saying so.

git.autoFetchMinutes.description: Fetch the current branch's remote every this many minutes, so the status bar's incoming count stays current. 0 (the default) never fetches on its own: Eludite makes no network call unless asked (PLAN.md section 2).

git.userName.description: The commit identity's name when neither the repository's config nor the global git config (`~/.gitconfig`) has `user.name`. The repository's and the global config win.

git.userEmail.description: The commit identity's email when neither the repository's config nor the global git config has `user.email`.

git.gpgSign.description: Commit signing. Only `never` exists: signing (GPG or SSH, `commit.gpgSign`) needs a signing program or key access outside libgit2 and a passphrase prompt, which a later brief adds; until then Eludite's commits are unsigned whatever `commit.gpgSign` says.

agents.default.description: The name of the agent the Agents window selects at start. Empty: the first one (the native Claude Code adapter when found).

agents.claudeCodeAdapterPath.description: The native Claude Code ACP adapter (`eludite-claude-acp`). Empty: beside the eludite executable, then PATH; the npx adapter is the fallback.

agents.custom.description: ACP agents added to the Agents window after the built-in ones; one with a built-in's name replaces it. Any ACP agent speaking JSON-RPC on stdio works. Edited in the file (the Options dialog shows the count). When neither settings file has this key, the older `agents.json` in the config directory is read instead.

command.description: The executable (a path, or a name looked up on PATH).

browser.engine.description: Which browser the Web Browser window and the browser tools (eludite.browser.*) use. `embedded`: Eludite's own Chromium, drawn inside the Web Browser window: the `eludite-chromium` engine with CEF, which tools/cef/fetch.sh downloads (then build the engine with `cargo build -p eludite-chromium --features eludite-chromium/cef`); while either is missing, the tools use the external Chrome and the window says what to run. `external`: a Chrome or Chromium process with its own window (browser.chromePath). Applies to the next launch: a running browser of the other kind is closed.

browser.enginePath.description: The `eludite-chromium` executable of the embedded engine (browser.engine `embedded`). Empty: ELUDITE_CHROMIUM, then `eludite-chromium` beside the eludite executable (a packaged Eludite: tools/package/linux.sh lays it out), then cargo's build folder in a development build. CEF's files are then looked for beside the engine (`libcef.so` in its folder, or in `cef/` beside it), at CEF_PATH, then in tools/cef/fetch.sh's cache. Searched when the Web Browser window or a browser command first needs the engine, never at startup. Applies to the next launch.

browser.allowNoSandbox.description: Let the embedded engine run without Chromium's sandbox in this workspace when the sandbox cannot start: neither unprivileged user namespaces nor the setuid `chrome-sandbox` helper beside `libcef.so` is available, or Eludite runs as root. The engine still runs sandboxed whenever it can. Off: the engine refuses to start there, and the Web Browser window says how to enable the sandbox (`sudo chown root:root chrome-sandbox && sudo chmod 4755 chrome-sandbox`, or allowing user namespaces) and offers this opt-in once. While the engine runs without the sandbox, the Web Browser window shows it in a strip and the audit log records the start (`eludite.browser.engine_start`, `sandbox: none`). Kept in the workspace's `.eludite/settings.json`; ELUDITE_CHROME_NO_SANDBOX=1 in Eludite's environment (tests, CI) is the only other way. Applies to the next launch.
browser.allowNoSandbox.x-eludite-label: Run without Chromium's sandbox for this workspace

browser.useBuiltIn.description: Open the page of a web project that starts (its launch profile's `launchBrowser` and `launchUrl`) in the Web Browser window, as a tab agents can read and drive (eludite.browser.*): Debug > Open in Web Browser Window. Takes effect while the embedded engine is found (browser.engine `embedded` with `eludite-chromium` and CEF present); otherwise, or off, the page opens in the system browser. Applies to the next start.
browser.useBuiltIn.x-eludite-label: Open web projects in the Web Browser window

browser.homePage.description: The page a new tab of the Web Browser window opens (Ctrl+T, the + button) and the Home button goes to. A url (`http://localhost:5000/`) or `about:blank`.

browser.showDevToolsTab.description: Open DevTools as a second tab beside every page tab the Web Browser window opens. Off: DevTools opens only on F12, the toolbar's DevTools button, the context menu's Inspect or eludite.browser.devtools.

browser.chromePath.description: The Chrome or Chromium executable the browser tools (eludite.browser.*) launch. Empty: Chrome for Testing from tools/chrome/fetch.sh in Eludite's cache, then google-chrome, google-chrome-stable, chromium, chromium-browser or chrome on PATH, then the platform's usual install locations. Applies to the next launch.

browser.headless.description: Run the browser without a window (Chrome's --headless=new). Off: the browser opens its own window beside Eludite, so you see what agents do. Applies to the next launch.

browser.viewport.description: The browser window's size at launch, WIDTHxHEIGHT in pixels (Chrome's --window-size). A tab's viewport can be changed later with eludite.browser.resize. Applies to the next launch.

terminal.defaultProfile.description: The profile New Terminal (Ctrl+Shift+`), View > Terminal (Ctrl+`) and eludite.terminal.open without a `profile` start: a name from the Terminal window's dropdown (`bash`, `zsh`, `fish`, `sh`; `Developer PowerShell`, `PowerShell`, `Command Prompt` on Windows; or one of terminal.profiles). Empty: the platform's default, $SHELL on Linux and macOS (else `sh`) and Developer PowerShell on Windows (PowerShell when no Build Tools are located).

terminal.profiles.description: Profiles added to the Terminal window's dropdown after the built-in ones; one with a built-in's name replaces it. Each runs `command` (a path, or a name looked up on PATH) with `args` and extra `env`, in the workspace's folder unless `cwd` (absolute, or relative to the workspace) says otherwise. Edited in the file (the Options dialog shows the count).

command.description: The shell's executable (a path, or a name looked up on PATH).

cwd.description: The starting folder, absolute or relative to the workspace's folder.

terminal.fontSize.description: The terminal's font size in pixels (Visual Studio's 10 points at 96 DPI is 13). The font is Cascadia Mono where installed, else the editor's monospace font.

terminal.scrollback.description: Lines each terminal keeps above its screen. 10,000 lines take under 20 MB per terminal. Applies to terminals opened after the change.

terminal.copyOnSelect.description: Copy the selection to the clipboard as soon as the mouse button is released. Off (Visual Studio's default): Ctrl+C with a selection, Ctrl+Shift+C or Ctrl+Insert copies.

terminal.bell.description: What a terminal's bell (BEL) does: `visual` flashes the terminal's frame (the default; Visual Studio makes no sound), `none` ignores it.

terminal.inheritToolPaths.description: Put the folders of the tools Eludite located first on the terminal's PATH, once each: the `dotnet` it builds with (and DOTNET_ROOT), Cargo's bin folder, and Node.js when located, so `dotnet --version` in the terminal prints the SDK Eludite uses (Visual Studio's Developer PowerShell does the same with its own tools). Off: the terminal inherits Eludite's environment unchanged. Applies to terminals opened after the change.
terminal.inheritToolPaths.x-eludite-label: Add Eludite's located tools to PATH

terminal.shellIntegration.description: Source a small script into bash, zsh, fish and PowerShell that marks each prompt and each command's start, end and exit code (OSC 133) and reports the current folder (OSC 7): agents' eludite.terminal.wait with `prompt` then answers the command's exit code, and links resolve against the folder you `cd` into. It never changes your dotfiles: the script is passed through the shell's startup options (`--rcfile`, `ZDOTDIR`, fish's `--init-command`, PowerShell's `-NoExit -Command`) and then runs your own startup files. Off, or with another shell: a prompt is recognized by a heuristic. Applies to terminals opened after the change.

search.excludes.description: Globs of files and folders Find in Files and Replace in Files skip (brief 0042), matched against the path inside the searched folder as `.gitignore` patterns are; a folder that matches is not entered. Edited in the file (the Options dialog shows the count).

search.useGitignore.description: Skip what `.gitignore` files (and `.git/info/exclude` and the global excludes file) ignore, as `git` and ripgrep do. Off: only search.excludes applies.

search.maxFileSize.description: Files larger than this many megabytes are not searched (generated bundles, data files). An open document is searched whatever its size.

search.followSymlinks.description: Follow symbolic links to folders and files while searching. Off (the default) skips them, so a link cannot make a search visit a folder twice or leave the workspace.
